title: Agentic Incident Response through Digital Twin-Enhanced Multiscale Planning
blurb: This paper introduces an agentic incident-response system that splits planning across two scales: a decision-theoretic rollout planner allocates security resources at the tactical level, while a lightweight LLM agent translates that strategy into executable recovery commands. A digital twin drives both tactical simulation and operational emulation, avoiding the hallucination and short planning horizons of repeated LLM calls. Across three attack scenarios, the approach cut recovery execution time by 15.1% and raised recovery rate by 33.6% over frontier LLM baselines.

title: Microsoft confirms an AI worm is propagating through Copilot and other MS apps
blurb: Microsoft confirmed an AI worm demonstrated by researcher Håkon Måløy that hides instructions in Word documents, using Copilot as the propagation vector to alter figures and copy itself into new Copilot-generated files. Microsoft says it addressed the findings via coordinated disclosure and layered safeguards, but the underlying prompt-injection class stays unfixable because models still cannot reliably separate instructions from data.

title: Microsoft almost gave away the keys to everyone’s Azure Cosmos DBs
blurb: Wiz disclosed a critical flaw in Azure Cosmos DB's Gremlin API that exposed the Cosmos Master Key, granting read and write access to any customer database plus a directory of every database on the service with subscription and tenant IDs. Microsoft shipped a hot fix within two days of the November 2025 report but spent eight months re-engineering the infrastructure to remove the master key and add guardrails; there is no evidence of exploitation before the fix.

title: TrainShield: Targeted Awareness for Cybersecurity Training
blurb: This paper introduces TrainShield, a training paradigm that embeds adaptive security lessons directly into user workflows, triggering context-specific micro-learning the moment real-time detection flags a risk like phishing or data loss. Detected events map to LLM-generated training instances tuned to the user's knowledge level, converting live incidents into immediate teachable moments rather than deferring to periodic modules. A preliminary study found users preferred it over lengthy asynchronous training, though aligning generated content with user expectations remains a challenge.

title: VulnGym: Benchmarking Coding Agents for Repository-Level Vulnerability Detection
blurb: VulnGym is a new benchmark that evaluates whether coding agents can find vulnerabilities across full repositories rather than preselected code snippets, aligning 184 reviewed GitHub advisories with their vulnerable repo versions and annotating 408 entries with line-level entry points, critical operations, and vulnerability traces. Across the end-to-end task and three oracle-based subtasks, the authors find current agents perform poorly at both repository-level detection and constructing accurate supporting traces, a caution for teams considering agentic code review as a primary triage layer.

title: How companies could share cyber risks without exposing their secrets
blurb: This op-ed argues that zero-knowledge proofs could let infrastructure operators prove a vulnerability is present without exposing the asset inventories, network diagrams, and scan data that would otherwise become an attacker roadmap. Existing information-sharing programs cover incident indicators and defensive advice but rarely pre-incident vulnerability and configuration data, which firms guard because once it leaves, it can be breached, subpoenaed, or repurposed by regulators.

title: Solving the Shortest Vector Problem in time $2^{0.6039n}$ Time via Mid-point Hessian
blurb: A new paper presents randomized algorithms that solve the Shortest Vector Problem in $2^{0.6039n}$ time classically and $2^{0.5411n}$ quantumly, down from the $2^{n}$ time and space of the 2015 Aggarwal-Dadush-Regev-Stephens-Davidowitz result. SVP hardness underpins the lattice-based schemes now standardized for post-quantum crypto, including ML-KEM and ML-DSA, so faster solvers chip at their concrete security margins. The technique estimates the Hessian of the periodic Gaussian at the half-vector to identify the parity class of a shortest vector.

title: Web security is too hard
blurb: A security engineer walks through a legitimate Cloudflare Wallet launch and shows that its onboarding flow is indistinguishable from a consent-phishing attack: manufactured urgency to claim a handle, an OAuth authorization prompt, and an entry point on a separate cloudflare.pay domain that anyone can spoof for $20. The takeaway for defenders is that when vendors ship flows that violate their own anti-phishing guidance, user training collapses, and only fundamentals like enforced SSO, scoped OAuth grants, and domain allowlisting hold up.

title: When Vibe Hacking Turns AI into the Junior Hacker Every Adversary Always Wanted
blurb: Vibe hacking" lets low-skill attackers use LLMs to close knowledge gaps and reach operational capability, expanding the population of capable adversaries.

title: How Palo Alto Wants AI to Patch Cyber Threats in Hours
blurb: Palo Alto Networks launched an AI-powered security platform that aims to detect vulnerabilities and deploy protections in hours rather than weeks. CEO Nikesh Arora framed the release as fighting AI with AI, and predicted enterprises will eventually spend as much as 15% of operating expenses on AI.

title: Microsoft reduces NuGet API keys to just 30 days, here's why
blurb: Microsoft cut NuGet API key lifetimes to 30 days to shrink the window for leaked-credential abuse, with further reductions possible.

title: A Multi-Objective AutoML-based Efficient Intrusion Detection System for EV Charging Networks
blurb: This paper proposes an AutoML intrusion detection system for EV charging networks that jointly optimizes detection accuracy, inference latency, and model size.

title: Apple launches legal challenge against the UK government
blurb: Apple filed a legal challenge against the UK government over the Home Office's repeated demands to build a backdoor into its end-to-end encrypted user data. The case escalates a dispute running since early 2025, with encryption experts calling the request technically unworkable and Apple maintaining its refusal to weaken encryption for law enforcement access.

title: N-able Says Attackers Take Over N-central Servers After Initial Fix Proves Incomplete
blurb: N-able confirmed attackers exploited an authentication bypass in its N-central RMM platform to gain remote administrative access, then pivoted through the built-in Take Control tool to install persistent Cloudflare tunnels on managed endpoints. The initial fix was incomplete, so every customer must move to build 2026.3.1.7, released August 2, and separately hunt for and remove the tunnel services, which survive the N-central upgrade.

title: Google Password Manager Attacks Could Let Malware Hijack Passkey-Protected Accounts
blurb: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 detailed three post-compromise techniques, dubbed Pass-ta-key, against Chrome's Google Password Manager on Windows, letting malware already on a device silently obtain valid authentication assertions or extract the Security Domain Secret that decrypts a victim's synced passkeys. None of the paths break the underlying cryptography or carry a CVE, but the strongest give attackers reusable access to passkey-protected accounts from their own environment after the initial endpoint compromise.

title: N-able warns of N-central auth bypass flaw exploited in attacks
blurb: N-able warned that attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-18577, an authentication bypass in its N-central RMM platform that enables administrative account takeover across both hosted and on-premises servers. The flaw stems from an incomplete patch for an earlier bypass, and because N-central is the tool MSPs use to manage large multi-OS fleets, a compromise lets attackers pivot well beyond N-able's direct customers.

title: Decades-Old BMC Vulnerability Exposes Thousands of Data Centers to Attacks
blurb: Security firm Lava reported that nearly 37,000 internet-exposed BMC management interfaces are vulnerable to CVE-2013-4786, a 22-year-old IPMI flaw that leaks password hashes for offline cracking, with over 24,000 disclosing authentication hashes before login. BMCs are among the most privileged control points in a data center, letting attackers who crack weak or default credentials power-cycle hosts, push firmware, and alter low-level platform configuration.

title: TP-Link Omada ZTP Vulnerabilities Chain Into Full Network Takeover
blurb: Forescout disclosed 15 vulnerabilities in the zero-touch provisioning systems behind TP-Link's Omada networking line, 11 of which received CVEs, and chained several with two prior RCE flaws to demonstrate full takeover of the controllers that manage entire device fleets. The exposure is real for enterprise buyers, as Forescout found 1,800 Omada controllers reachable from the internet despite TP-Link's guidance to keep them off the public web.

title: New DOUBLECUP ClickFix service hides malware in browser cache images
blurb: A Russian loader-as-a-service called DOUBLECUP, tracked by SOCRadar since early June 2026, uses ClickFix fake-CAPTCHA prompts to preload steganographic PNGs into browser cache and deliver CountLoader plus a new DeviceManager RAT to Windows and macOS. The service impersonates NetSuite, Odoo, HubSpot, and Salesforce login pages, handling the hosting, encryption, and payload rebuilds while customers supply only the malicious front-end sites.

title: 77 Open VSX extensions found harvesting developer info
blurb: Manifold Security found 77 malicious extensions on the Open VSX marketplace impersonating legitimate developer tools from vendors including AMD, Azure, and Salesforce, all exfiltrating system and development-environment metadata to a shared domain, mangorbit[.]com. Published between July 26 and August 1, 2026, the "evil twin" packages harvested hostname, Git repository, and CI data but did not touch source code, credentials, or authentication tokens.

title: Massive ChainDrop npm supply-chain attack infects hundreds of packages
blurb: A self-propagating worm named ChainDrop compromised at least 868 npm packages across 1,381 versions, including widely used caching utilities like Keyv and Cacheable that total roughly 2 billion monthly downloads. Because the malicious releases were built through legitimate GitHub Actions workflows, they carried valid provenance, letting the infostealer harvest developer and cloud credentials from any environment that ran npm install against an affected version.

title: New cPanel Critical Flaw Could Let Hosting Customers Run SQL as Database Root
blurb: cPanel patched CVE-2026-58048, a critical flaw (CVSS 9.4) that let an authenticated hosting customer execute SQL in the database's root context, bypassing the privilege boundary between a cPanel account and the server's administrative database identity. The bug affects all supported versions of cPanel & WHM plus WP Squared, can extend to full operating-system compromise depending on configuration, and admins who cannot patch immediately can temporarily revoke the MySQL feature from users.

title: New Pass-ta-key attacks let malware hijack Google-synced passkeys
blurb: Palo Alto Networks' Unit 42 disclosed "Pass-ta-key," three attacks that let malware already running on a compromised Windows device abuse Google Password Manager's synced passkeys to hijack accounts, bypass user verification, and extract private keys without admin rights or biometrics. The attacks don't break passkey cryptography but exploit how Chrome and Google's cloud authenticator handle device trust, and they succeed against services like eBay that fail to validate the User Verified flag.

title: Data Centers Exposed US Telecoms to China Hacks, US Panel to Say
blurb: A forthcoming House committee report concludes that US telecom carriers connected their networks to data centers and related infrastructure in ways that created cybersecurity gaps, likely enabling the Salt Typhoon campaign that breached several mobile operators two years ago. The finding puts scrutiny on how carriers architect data-center interconnects and hardens the case for tighter federal security requirements across enterprise telecom procurement.

title: Lost in Permissions: Exploring the Microsoft 365 App Ecosystem
blurb: A new academic paper presents the first systematic security measurement of the Microsoft 365 third-party app ecosystem, crawling over 8,000 marketplace applications. The authors find that only 1,069 disclose both descriptions and permission sets, and that many request overly broad tenant-wide scopes like directory-wide read/write access in violation of least-privilege principles. For IT admins, the takeaway is that OAuth grants in the M365 marketplace are inconsistently disclosed and frequently over-privileged, expanding the tenant attack surface.

title: ExfilSquad hackers leak info of over 100,000 UK police officers, staff
blurb: A cyberattack on the U.K.'s Police National Legal Database exposed the names, organizations, and email addresses of more than 100,000 police officers, staff, and criminal justice professionals, with the ExfilSquad extortion group claiming 135,000 stolen records. The National Crime Agency and Information Commissioner's Office are investigating, though PNLD says no passwords, credentials, or confidential victim data were compromised.

title: Russian spies turn public Wi-Fi into malware delivery systems
blurb: Russia's SVR is compromising public Wi-Fi networks near targets to intercept traffic and push malware onto devices as they connect, according to reporting on the intelligence service's surveillance tactics. Enterprise security teams face renewed pressure to enforce always-on VPNs and certificate pinning for traveling and remote staff, since any untrusted network now doubles as a potential adversary-controlled delivery channel.

title: Feds get 3 days to patch N-able God mode flaw under active exploit
blurb: CISA added an actively exploited N-able N-central vulnerability to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog and gave federal agencies three days to patch, far shorter than the standard 21-day window. The flaw grants full administrative control over the RMM platform that MSPs use to manage client fleets, so a single compromise cascades downstream to every customer environment N-central touches.

title: Retirement of Azure DevOps issuer in Workload identity federation service connections
blurb: Microsoft is deprecating the Azure DevOps issuer in workload identity federation service connections, with retirement set for July 1, 2027, as it standardizes on the Microsoft Entra issuer across Azure. Teams running secretless Azure Pipelines on single-tenant Entra apps or managed identities in the public cloud must migrate their federated credentials off the vstoken.dev.azure.com prefix, though multi-tenant apps and non-public clouds are excluded for now.

title: Google ADK flaws reveal what happens when AI agents trust the wrong message
blurb: Pillar Security disclosed flaws in the GitHub workflows for Google's Agent Development Kit for Python, where prompt injections in external pull requests and public issues could induce triage agents to trigger privileged automation, enabling manipulated PR approvals and extraction of the adk-bot token and a Google Cloud service account key. Google has since removed the affected workflows and hardened the repository, but the case shows agent-to-agent handoffs can escalate privileges past conventional identity and CI/CD controls.

title: CISA Adds Exploited N-able N-central Flaw to KEV After Customer Compromises
blurb: CISA added CVE-2026-18577, a CVSS 8.2 authentication-bypass flaw in N-able N-central, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after Huntress reported active exploitation across multiple organizations. The bug is an incomplete fix for CVE-2026-18556 and lets remote attackers gain admin access, then abuse the built-in Take Control feature to pivot into managed endpoints, so MSPs running versions below 2026.3 HF1 should patch and hunt for the published indicators of compromise.

title: Hotel Wi-Fi attacks use custom malware to breach Microsoft 365 accounts
blurb: Microsoft attributed a global campaign called CaptiveCrunch to Russian threat actor Midnight Blizzard, which manipulates DNS settings on hotel and conference Wi-Fi captive portals to redirect users to fake Microsoft 365 login and Entra ID device-code phishing pages. The operation deploys two new Windows malware families, CornFlake and ChocoShell, that steal Microsoft 365 session tokens and browser credentials, giving IT teams a fresh reason to enforce phishing-resistant MFA for traveling employees.

title: MSPs urged to patch immediately after N-able issues hotfix for N-central ‘god mode’ flaw
blurb: N-able released a hotfix for CVE-2026-18577, a critical authentication bypass in its N-central remote management platform that grants unauthenticated "god mode" access across every downstream endpoint an affected server manages. Huntress reports active exploitation in the wild, so on-prem MSPs should patch immediately or take N-central offline, while hosted instances were mitigated automatically by N-able.

title: Visual screenshots now included in Google Meet meeting notes
blurb: Google added automatic screenshot capture of presented content to Google Meet's "Take notes for me" feature, embedding visuals of charts and slides directly into the AI-generated notes document alongside the transcript. Admins control the rollout through the Admin console, choosing to always allow screenshots or only when recording is enabled, with availability limited to Business Standard and Plus, Enterprise Standard and Plus, and Google AI Pro for Education tiers.

title: Cloudflare has mostly ditched third party security tools, suggests not trying that at home
blurb: Cloudflare disclosed that it now runs most of its own security stack in-house rather than buying third-party tools, then explicitly warned that most enterprises should not copy the approach. The caveat is the real signal for IT buyers: Cloudflare's build-over-buy economics depend on in-house security engineering depth most shops lack, so the vendor-consolidation lesson here is about capability, not just license spend.

title: DDoS against Norwegian government IT infrastructure – status
blurb: Norway's Digitalisation Agency (Digdir) reported a DDoS attack against its national digital-identity and public-service platforms, including ID-porten, Altinn, MinID, and Maskinporten, with status updates posted to its incident page. The outage temporarily blocked citizen and business access to authentication and government eServices that most Norwegian public agencies and banks depend on for login, underscoring the concentration risk of routing an entire country's identity layer through one provider.

title: Cortex Framework v7 is GA: Build agentic workflows without disrupting SAP operations
blurb: Google Cloud made Cortex Framework v7 generally available, adding purpose-built SAP data product accelerators that deploy in BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog to feed the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform without disrupting core ERP operations. Enterprises running SAP can now expose transactional data as AI-ready, semantically labeled products orchestrated through Dataform, letting agents act on business context without a separate data-modeling project or added infrastructure overhead.

title: Texas slams on the brakes for 1,800 data centers, power grid requirements are five times higher than peak record demand — 474 gigawatts of power requests are now subject to new moratorium
blurb: Texas Gov. Greg Abbott ordered a moratorium on new data center grid connections through PUCT and ERCOT until regulators audit the more than 1,800 pending projects, which together request 474 gigawatts, five times the state's peak recorded demand. The pause hits applicants that skipped a required survey on power, water, and tax-break usage, though projects outside ERCOT's territory or bringing their own generation can still proceed.

title: Future Mode Part 2: The foundation for securing agentic browsing
blurb: Google introduced the second part of its Chrome Enterprise "Future Mode" series, detailing security controls for agentic browsing that tie AI-agent actions to a signed-in employee's corporate identity and existing Chrome policies. The setup lets browser-based agents complete multi-step tasks like invoice reconciliation and candidate sourcing while enterprise data-protection rules apply to both the human and the agent acting on their behalf.

title: AMD unveils AI GPU to challenge Nvidia’s Rubin
blurb: AMD introduced the Instinct MI455X, a CDNA 5 accelerator with 432GB of HBM4 and up to 40 petaflops of FP4 compute that will anchor its 72-GPU Helios rack platform against Nvidia's Rubin and DGX systems. AMD trails on peak compute, roughly 40 versus Rubin's 50 petaflops, but leads on memory capacity and bandwidth, giving enterprise buyers a credible second source as HBM shortages tighten supply.

title: Iran Cyberattacks Against Minnesota Water Systems
blurb: Suspected Iranian cyberattacks hit water utilities in Minnesota and at least six other states, with attribution still preliminary and no confirmed physical damage so far. The campaign puts renewed scrutiny on OT and SCADA security across municipal water systems, where legacy control networks and thin IT budgets leave critical infrastructure operators exposed to state-linked intrusions.

title: ServiceNow debuts six autonomous security products built on Armis and Veza
blurb: ServiceNow launched six autonomous security products and a set of AI agents that carry vulnerability and incident work to closure without an analyst driving each step, built on its $7.75B Armis and $1.3B Veza acquisitions. The lineup extends the Autonomous Security & Risk portfolio into exposure management, detection, cyber-physical coverage from Armis, and AI-agent access control from Veza, targeting enterprises that juggle 70-plus disconnected security tools.

title: Apple launches fresh legal challenge against UK encrypted data access demand
blurb: Apple filed a fresh legal challenge against a UK Home Office order demanding backdoor access to British customers' encrypted iCloud data, a year after a broader demand covering American users collapsed under pressure from Trump and Vance. Apple has already disabled Advanced Data Protection for new UK users and will require existing users to turn it off, ceding cloud-encryption ground while it contests the Investigatory Powers Act notice.

title: AI agents get better at IT ops, but only with humans in the loop
blurb: A study by automation platform Fixify of nearly 147,000 real-world agent actions across 40 companies found AI agents now execute roughly one-third of enterprise IT tasks, concentrated in repeatable, low-risk software, security, and collaboration work. Human approval of AI-proposed actions climbed from 23% to 41% over three months as feedback loops improved, while analysts stay in the loop for identity, access provisioning, and other high-stakes changes.

title: Sources: the White House doesn't plan to publicly release its voluntary AI framework; details will be available to the companies that are part of the process (Maria Curi/Axios)
blurb: The White House does not plan to publicly release its voluntary AI framework, according to sources, instead sharing details only with the companies participating in the process. The closed approach limits enterprise IT leaders outside the working group to secondhand accounts of the standards their AI vendors are being asked to meet, leaving compliance and procurement teams without a public baseline to plan against.

title: Microsoft tells employees to stop tokenmaxxing, sets division-level AI budgets
blurb: Microsoft EVP Jay Parikh told employees in an internal email to curb AI token use, switched the company's default internal model to a cheaper OpenAI option, and imposed division-level token spending caps as of July 2026. The move puts Microsoft alongside Amazon, Meta, Walmart, and Citi in throttling employee AI spend, treating token-priced tools as a metered utility bill rather than the seat-based licenses finance teams know how to budget.

title: US mulling ban on key Chinese networking tech in data center component crackdown — White House wants to impose restrictions in 2026, China says it will respond if necessary
blurb: The FCC is drafting a rule to ban imports of Chinese-made optical transceivers, the light-based data-center components where Innolight alone holds 27% of the global market, with the administration targeting an effective date before the end of the year. U.S. suppliers like Lumentum, Coherent, and Applied Optoelectronics can't yet match that scale, so enterprises building out data centers face supply-chain risk and likely higher networking costs.

title: AI incidents cost enterprises $2M or more, and the biggest shadow AI culprit is IT
blurb: Enterprise AI incidents now cost $2M or more per event, according to a WitnessAI survey, and 47% of IT decision-makers named their own IT and infrastructure teams as the top source of unsanctioned shadow AI. The finding shifts the governance problem inward, putting pressure on CIOs to inventory and gate the AI tools their own departments deploy rather than treating shadow AI as a business-user issue.

title: NVMe polishes its specs, brings virtualization to locally attached SSDs
blurb: The NVM Express consortium ratified new specifications that extend SR-IOV-style virtualization to locally attached SSDs, letting a single physical drive present multiple isolated NVMe controllers to VMs and containers without a hypervisor storage layer in the path. The update targets enterprise virtualization and multi-tenant hosts, giving IT teams direct-attached NVMe performance with the partitioning previously reserved for SAN and NVMe-oF deployments.

title: Real-world mainframe modernization with AI: A safe, scalable path from mainframe to cloud
blurb: Google Cloud argues that enterprise mainframe modernization is not a COBOL-to-Java code conversion problem but a data and dependency problem, spanning non-relational formats like VSAM and IMS, CICS transaction monitors, and proprietary protocols that AI agents can't natively read. Its pitch pairs Gemini for code understanding with mainframe-specific tooling across four pillars, emphasizing iterative migration validated against production traffic over a high-risk "big bang" cutover.

title: Unifying public and private data: Scale knowledge graphs with Data Commons on Spanner
blurb: Google made Data Commons on Spanner Graph generally available and opened a preview of the new Data Commons Platform, letting enterprises join their private data with public knowledge graphs spanning 400B+ data points from over 100 sources including the UN, World Bank, and WHO. Moving off the old Bigtable caching layer to native Spanner Graph adds SQL-like graph queries, multi-region consistency, and MCP tool access for connecting internal records to normalized public reference data.

title: Cloud giants pour nearly $600B into capex as AI demand surges
blurb: The major cloud providers are on track to spend nearly $600B in combined capital expenditure this year, driven by sustained AI compute demand as quarterly cloud revenue climbs past $143B. Enterprise buyers should expect continued capacity expansion from Microsoft, Google, and Amazon, though the scale of the buildout raises the question of whether the spending converts to durable margins rather than pricing relief for customers.

title: AI helps Microsoft bug hunters chase a record $20M payday
blurb: Microsoft's bug bounty payouts are on track to hit a record $20M this year as security researchers increasingly lean on AI tooling to surface vulnerabilities across Windows, Azure, and Microsoft 365 faster than manual review allows. The surge signals that AI-assisted vulnerability discovery is now material to enterprise patch cadence, raising the odds that defenders and attackers alike find flaws before IT teams can deploy fixes.

title: UK mulls making employers ask before installing bossware
blurb: The UK government is considering rules that would require employers to consult staff before deploying employee-monitoring software, part of a broader review of workplace surveillance and automated decision-making. IT leaders running tools like Microsoft Viva Insights, Teradata, or dedicated bossware would face new consultation and transparency obligations, adding a compliance step to any monitoring rollout across UK-based workforces.

title: Texas says data centers must pass an audit before connecting to the grid
blurb: Governor Greg Abbott directed ERCOT and the Public Utility Commission of Texas to audit new data center proposals before grid connection, requiring disclosure of incentives, grid reliance, water use, and community impact. The review adds a procurement hurdle in the second-largest US data center market, where ERCOT is weighing 474GW of connection requests, with data centers accounting for roughly 90% of new demand.

title: Samsung Reveals New 3D-Memory Roadmap in Bid for AI Tech Lead
blurb: Samsung shared its next-generation 3D-memory roadmap, promising higher performance and lower power draw as it works to overtake SK Hynix and Micron in AI memory. The move targets the high-bandwidth memory market where SK Hynix currently leads Nvidia's supply, and signals to enterprise buyers that a third credible HBM source is pushing to close the gap.

title: Introducing Database Operations Agents: The future of autonomous database management
blurb: Google Cloud introduced two AI-powered database agents at Cloud Next '26: a Database Onboarding Agent for Day 0 setup and configuration, and a Database Observability Agent for Day 1 and 2 monitoring, troubleshooting, and remediation via natural language. Both integrate across Chat, CLI, the Cloud console, MCP servers, and third-party IDEs, targeting the manual provisioning, query tuning, and diagnosis work that DBAs and SREs handle across the database lifecycle.

title: Cloud infrastructure spending just hit an eight-year high
blurb: Cloud infrastructure services spending hit $143B in Q2 2026, up $43B and marking an eight-year-high growth rate on an 11th straight quarter of expansion, with generative AI cited as the primary driver. AWS still leads at 28% share but Microsoft (20%) and Google Cloud (15%) are growing faster, and nine neoclouds including CoreWeave, Oracle, and Nscale now rank among the top 40 providers.

title: Obsidian Security raises $85M as AI agents create cybersecurity’s next major attack surface
blurb: Obsidian Security raised $85M in a Series D at a $1.1B post-money valuation, led by Crescent Cove Advisor with Greylock and Menlo Ventures participating, to secure the non-human identities that autonomous AI agents use to reach cloud and SaaS data. The round targets a gap traditional IAM tools were not built for, with Obsidian citing 65% of its enterprise customers already granting agents access to third-party SaaS.

title: Red Hat leads open-source project to automate AI governance
blurb: Red Hat launched asago, an open-source project that turns AI governance policies into operational controls by mapping them to frameworks like the NIST AI RMF, OWASP LLM Top 10, and EU AI Act, then generating Kubernetes, Terraform, and Ansible configs. The tool targets enterprises running long-lived AI agents in production, replacing manual policy interpretation and custom scripts with an auditable trail linking each control to its underlying requirement.

title: Senate set to debate package of bills on privacy, AI and kids safety
blurb: The Senate Commerce Committee will mark up five bills Wednesday covering online privacy, AI, and children's safety, led by the Kids Online Safety Act, which would impose a "reasonable care" duty on platforms handling data for users under 17 and empower the FTC to investigate and fine violators. KOSA drew earlier support from Apple and OpenAI but now faces opposition from roughly 100 groups after the House stripped its stronger duty-of-care language.

title: Data center energy constraints and moratoriums are mounting. Expect to see stalled AI projects
blurb: New York became the first state to impose a year-long moratorium on new data center construction, joining 127 other US jurisdictions with similar restrictions as energy costs and grid strain mount. At least 75 projects worth roughly $130B were blocked or delayed in Q1 2026, matching all of 2025 combined, which signals that enterprise AI buildouts now face permitting and power risk alongside chip supply.

title: Apple plans to open iPhone clipboard access to Windows PCs
blurb: Apple agreed to develop a solution that lets iPhones sync clipboard content with paired Windows PCs, responding to a Microsoft interoperability request filed under the EU's DMA. The feature would extend Universal Clipboard-style copy-paste across the Apple-Microsoft device boundary, though Apple warned it may limit the capability to the EU and could still abandon it on operating-system integrity or IP grounds.

title: Your Azure DevOps pipelines have a 2027 deadline, and the clock has just started
blurb: Microsoft deprecated the Azure DevOps issuer for workload identity federation on July 1, 2026, with full retirement set for July 1, 2027, and every Azure Pipelines Service Connection built before late 2025 needs migrating to the Entra issuer or it stops authenticating to Azure. The portal converts connections one at a time, so shops with hundreds of single-tenant connections in the public cloud will need to script the undocumented MigrateToEntraIssuer REST call to finish before the deadline.

title: Microsoft almost gave away the keys to everyone’s Azure Cosmos DBs
blurb: Wiz disclosed a critical Azure Cosmos DB flaw in its Gremlin API that could have exposed a Cosmos Master Key, granting read and write access to any customer's database plus a directory of every account's subscription and tenant IDs. Microsoft shipped a hotfix within two days but needed eight months to re-engineer the service, removing the master key and adding new guardrails to the NoSQL database that underpins much of Azure.

title: Microsoft brings Azure Linux 4.0 to Windows PCs through WSL
blurb: Microsoft made Azure Linux 4.0 available as a WSL distribution, letting Windows developers run the same OS locally that backs Azure Kubernetes Service and other cloud workloads. The move gives enterprises dev-to-prod parity without a separate VM or container setup, tightening Microsoft's grip on teams already standardized on Azure and Windows.

title: Rubrik unveils Agent Identity to govern AI agents one tool call at a time
blurb: Rubrik released Agent Identity at Black Hat, a service that governs AI agents by granting scoped, short-lived access one tool call at a time through an MCP gateway rather than letting agents inherit humans' standing permissions. The service extends Rubrik Agent Cloud into the credential layer and enters the crowded agent-authorization market alongside Entra, Okta, and Auth0, targeting IT teams that report low visibility into the agents already running in their environments.

title: Nutanix to slash 5% of global workforce as part of ‘business structure’ review
blurb: Nutanix will cut about 5% of its global workforce as part of a business-structure review, taking up to $43M in pre-tax charges by the end of October. The cuts come despite a strong Q3 fiscal 2026 with revenue up 10% to $703M and 700-plus new logo wins driven by VMware customers defecting after Broadcom's acquisition.

title: Broadcom cannot use US legal privilege to block EU probes, court rules
blurb: The EU General Court dismissed Broadcom's bid to block the European Commission from accessing U.S. legal documents in its VMware antitrust probe, ruling that companies cannot invoke American legal professional privilege to withhold materials from EU investigators. The precedent removes a shield multinationals hoped to use against Brussels and keeps the Commission's inquiry into Broadcom's VMware licensing and partner-program changes on track.

title: How Palo Alto Wants AI to Patch Cyber Threats in Hours
blurb: Palo Alto Networks introduced an AI-powered security platform that detects vulnerabilities and deploys protections in hours rather than weeks, with CEO Nikesh Arora framing it as fighting AI attacks with AI defense. Arora expects enterprises to eventually spend as much as 15% of operating expenses on AI, a projection that reshapes security procurement math and pressures point-tool vendors selling slower detection-and-response workflows.

title: How we built a software factory to drive Astro’s GitHub issue count to zero
blurb: Cloudflare ran an automated triage pipeline on the Astro repository for several months, using isolated AI subagents in GitHub Actions to reproduce bugs in sandboxes, diagnose root causes, and ship preview releases for reporters to verify. The engine became Flue, an open framework for building the same agent automation. Open issues dropped from over 200 to about 30 without auto-closing cold tickets, with zero expected within a month, which would be a first in the repo's five-year history.

title: GEM Training: How Meta Doubled the Efficiency of Its LLM-Scale Ads Foundation Model
blurb: Meta detailed how it scaled GEM, the foundation model behind Instagram and Facebook ads recommendations, to LLM-scale training on several thousand latest-gen GPUs. The team doubled end-to-end efficiency to 20-25% Model FLOPs Utilization while growing training FLOPs 4x in 12 months, using custom recommendation kernels, MXFP8 precision, and topology-aware 5D parallelism. The writeup is a reminder that LLM training recipes do not transfer cleanly to trillion-parameter recommendation models.

title: Gateway API v1.6: TCPRoute and UDPRoute Graduate to Standard
blurb: Gateway API v1.6 promoted TCPRoute and UDPRoute to Standard on the v1 API, giving raw L4 TCP and UDP workloads like databases, DNS, and VoIP a portable way to route through a Gateway instead of falling back to plain Services or implementation-specific CRDs. The release also splits experimental resources into a separate gateway.networking.x-k8s.io API group, and deprecates the v1alpha2 route versions ahead of removal in a future release.

title: Researchers: ChainDrop, a Shai-Hulud-based worm, has compromised 1,300+ npm packages, like Keyv, Cacheable, and flat-cache, with a combined 2B monthly downloads (Bill Toulas/BleepingComputer)
blurb: Researchers found that ChainDrop, a worm built on the Shai-Hulud codebase, has compromised more than 1,300 npm packages including Keyv, Cacheable, and flat-cache, which together see 2B monthly downloads. The scale means most Node.js build pipelines likely pulled a poisoned version, so teams should pin lockfiles, audit recent installs, and rotate any credentials exposed during CI runs.

title: Run CI/CD for millions of repos — on your platform, on Cloudflare
blurb: Cloudflare launched a CI SDK built on Cloudflare Workflows, letting teams run build, lint, typecheck, test, and conditional-deploy steps directly on its platform, triggered by artifact push events wired through wrangler config. It pairs with Artifacts, Cloudflare's versioned code storage for millions of repos, and supports both platform-managed and customer-defined CI jobs running simultaneously, plus an optional AI review agent that self-heals broken build steps.

title: How to Run Isolated Tenant Kubernetes Clusters on Shared GPU Infrastructure
blurb: NVIDIA's developer blog documents a pattern for giving each team its own isolated Kubernetes control plane without splitting the underlying GPU hardware. The setup pairs vCluster, which provisions per-team API servers, CRDs, and RBAC indistinguishable from a dedicated cluster, with KAI Scheduler, which carves a shared GPU pool into per-team quotas. The tutorial runs three tenant clusters on a single NVIDIA L40S, and the authors note the same queue hierarchy and node pool scale to hundreds of GPU nodes and dozens of teams.

title: Keyv and friends compromised in active Shai-Hulud supply chain attack
blurb: Attackers compromised the maintainer's GitHub account behind keyv and its sibling caching libraries, then pushed a malicious preinstall dropper and cut fresh npm releases signed by GitHub Actions, spreading the Shai-Hulud worm across at least 434 packages with over 2 billion monthly installs. The payload harvests environment secrets and exfiltrates them to public GitHub repos, so any recent npm install pulling flat-cache, file-entry-cache, or cacheable is a potential credential leak.

title: Control Reliability Engineering (CRE): Applying SRE Principles to Cybersecurity Controls
blurb: Phil Venables argues that most breaches trace to security controls that were assumed operational but were actually broken or misconfigured when needed, and proposes Control Reliability Engineering (CRE) to fix it. The framework ports SRE discipline directly onto security controls: SLIs and SLOs to define a healthy control, error budgets to govern acceptable decay, and continuous control monitoring plus root-cause analysis to catch drift before an attacker does.

title: Introducing: Cloudflare Agents
blurb: Cloudflare launched Cloudflare Agents, a management layer for hosted agents on Workers, starting with agent tracing that measures every model call, tool execution, and token spent per turn. The tracing works with OpenTelemetry-compatible harnesses including Think, Flue, and the AI SDK, surfacing agent-level failures like wrong tool choices, stale subagent context, and retry loops that return HTTP 200 but still fail.

title: AtumAI: A Principled Framework for Agentic Generation of Datacenter Control-Plane Policies
blurb: This paper introduces AtumAI, a framework that uses agentic AI to generate datacenter control-plane policies for workload placement, resource scaling, and power management from a plain-language goal. It compiles the request into a machine-checkable spec, then searches the design space with a diffusion model, evolutionary algorithm, and surrogate model, producing policies that outperform expert-engineered baselines while cutting new-task onboarding from months to a description.

title: Decades-Old BMC Vulnerability Exposes Thousands of Data Centers to Attacks
blurb: Data center security firm Lava reported that CVE-2013-4786, a 22-year-old flaw in the IPMI 2.0 authentication protocol, exposes roughly 37,000 internet-facing BMCs by leaking password-derived hashes for offline cracking. Because IPMI, Redfish, and the web console often share one credential database, a cracked hash unlocks the data center's most privileged control plane, and Lava found thousands of hosts already accepting empty usernames or default passwords.

title: AWS’s Kiro Crew aims to turn AI coding agents into autonomous engineering teams
blurb: AWS released Kiro Crew, an open-source orchestration platform that coordinates multiple AI coding agents across repositories and sessions to run long-running engineering work like incident investigation, PR monitoring, and ticket triage. It ships with persistent memory, approval workflows, scheduling, and security controls such as sandboxing and signed audit logs, and deploys entirely inside customer environments (laptops, containers, or VMs) with no AWS account required.

title: Scaling Kubernetes pods with KEDA based on Amazon SQS queue depth
blurb: This tutorial walks through autoscaling event-driven workers on Amazon EKS with KEDA, using SQS queue depth as the scaling signal instead of CPU or memory. It covers wiring KEDA to SQS via IRSA or EKS Pod Identity, how the operator translates backlog into HPA replica counts, and tuning queueLength, activationQueueLength, and cooldowns to control burst response. The payoff is autoscaling tied to actual outstanding work: faster spike handling and lower idle cost when queues drain.

title: You can’t debug what you can’t see — Observability for AI Agents
blurb: The author argues that standard APM misses the failure modes that matter for AI agents, which loop, hallucinate, and burn tokens without ever throwing a stack trace. The post lays out three pillars for agent observability: nested Langfuse traces capturing every model call, tool invocation, and sub-agent delegation; per-session and per-agent cost tracking to catch geometric token burn early; and proactive budget guardrails, since a tight loop can drain spend in seconds. Trace delivery stays non-blocking via a batch exporter, so an unreachable backend costs telemetry, not availability.

title: The Agent Development Lifecycle has arrived on Cloudflare
blurb: Cloudflare introduced a set of tools that let coding agents own more of the software development lifecycle beyond implementation, including @cloudflare/ci for self-healing CI/CD across millions of repos built on Workflows, OpenTelemetry traces in local dev via Wrangler, and Agent Traces for observing running agents. The pitch is that agents already overwhelm reviewers, mergers, and on-call engineers downstream, so Cloudflare is giving them the same production-grade observability and CI tooling their human counterparts rely on.

title: Cortex Framework v7 is GA: Build agentic workflows without disrupting SAP operations
blurb: Google Cloud made Cortex Framework v7 generally available, adding purpose-built data product accelerators that turn raw SAP ERP tables into semantically rich, agent-ready data products deployed directly in BigQuery and Knowledge Catalog. Orchestration now runs on Dataform for version-controlled, modular workflows, letting data teams feed Gemini Enterprise agents accurate business context without slowing mission-critical SAP operations or standing up separate pipeline infrastructure.

title: Your agent can now debug Workers with local tracing
blurb: Cloudflare's Wrangler and Vite dev servers now automatically capture OpenTelemetry traces for local Worker invocations and expose them to coding agents through a new Local Explorer API, requiring no SDK, config, or observability prompt. When the tooling detects an agent session, it points the agent to a read-only endpoint where it can query traces, correlated console logs, and local state in D1, KV, R2, Durable Objects, and Queues to find and verify fixes before deploying.

title: NVMe polishes its specs, brings virtualization to locally attached SSDs
blurb: The NVMe 2.2 spec adds live migration support, letting hypervisors move VMs across hosts without breaking locally attached SSD state.

title: Future Mode Part 2: The foundation for securing agentic browsing
blurb: Google detailed how Chrome Enterprise will secure agentic browsing, extending corporate identity, access policies, and data-loss controls to AI agents that log into SaaS apps and complete multi-step tasks on an employee's behalf. The pitch is that anchoring agent workflows inside the signed-in browser gives IT teams real-time context on open tabs and applications, narrowing the blast radius when an autonomous agent acts on enterprise data.

title: NVIDIA Vera Storage Benchmarks: Faster Encryption, Compression, Integrity Checking, and Recovery for AI-Native Storage
blurb: NVIDIA published benchmarks for its Vera BlueField-4 STX Storage Processor, showing the Vera CPU architecture outperforming x86 across encryption, integrity checking, compression, recovery, and a full multi-stage storage pipeline. The pitch is offloading CPU-side storage work in the agentic AI data path, where per-step operations across thousands of concurrent agents can bottleneck token generation, while cutting the core, power, and cooling overhead of scaling those functions on conventional CPUs.

title: How Cloudflare enforces engineering standards using AI
blurb: Cloudflare detailed how its AI code reviewer has flagged nearly 250,000 deviations from internal engineering standards and blocked 16,000 merges over four months, while a separate spec-reviewer agent has checked close to 600 technical designs before implementation. Both draw from the Cloudflare Codex, a governed set of RFC-formatted standards using RFC 2119 SHOULD/MUST keywords that both engineers and agents retrieve at the point of work. The trade-off is upfront governance overhead: each domain needs an owner accountable for content and consistency.

title: Introducing Database Operations Agents: The future of autonomous database management
blurb: Google Cloud released two AI-powered database agents at Cloud Next '26, splitting the lifecycle between a Database Onboarding Agent for Day 0 setup and configuration and a Database Observability Agent that lets SREs and DBAs diagnose and remediate issues through natural-language prompts. Both run across Chat, CLI, the Cloud console, and MCP servers, targeting the manual query-tuning and troubleshooting cycles that currently eat hours of on-call time.

title: Multiple result sets: How Database Migration Service automates SQL server to PostgreSQL translation
blurb: Google Cloud detailed how its Database Migration Service automatically translates SQL Server stored procedures that return multiple result sets into PostgreSQL equivalents, mapping them to SETOF REFCURSOR outputs based on result-set count and whether the procedure uses a scalar return value. The post walks through the conversion logic, a healthcare reporting example that returns up to four result sets plus a status integer, and how to run and test the generated PostgreSQL code.

title: Oligo Security raises $60M as AI speeds up exploit development
blurb: Oligo Security raised $60M to scale its runtime security platform, which uses an eBPF sensor to track which library functions a workload actually calls and blocks in-progress exploits at the application layer without killing the container. The pitch lands as automated exploit development compresses patch windows, and Oligo reports 300% ARR growth alongside a Series B valuation that has more than doubled since January 2025.

title: Show HN: NixOS-DGX-Spark – Nix and NixOS on the DGX Spark
blurb: A developer released NixOS-DGX-Spark, an open-source project that brings Nix and NixOS to NVIDIA's DGX Spark and the Asus Ascent GX10, shipping USB images and a NixOS hardware module with a custom NVIDIA-optimized kernel for full GPU and Ethernet support. Teams can run the Nix dev shells and playbooks directly on stock DGX OS via nix-gl-host, or install NixOS outright for reproducible CUDA environments after a required firmware update.

title: Your Azure DevOps pipelines have a 2027 deadline, and the clock has just started
blurb: Microsoft deprecated the Azure DevOps issuer for workload identity federation on July 1, 2026, giving teams until July 1, 2027 before Service Connections built on the old vstoken.dev.azure.com issuer stop authenticating to Azure. The portal migrates connections one at a time in a couple of minutes each, so orgs running hundreds will need the undocumented MigrateToEntraIssuer REST call, and only single-tenant Entra apps and Managed Identities in the public cloud are affected.

title: The development pipeline is a production system
blurb: The author argues that development pipelines deserve the same outage response as customer-facing production systems, since a broken build, failing test suite, or downed QA server stops the team from shipping just as surely as a service failure stops customers. The recommendation is to inventory every step from "customer wants something" to "delivered," from issue trackers and IDEs to CI/CD and package repositories, then treat any break in that chain as a top-priority incident rather than background toil.

title: Kubernetes v1.37 Sneak Peek
blurb: The Kubernetes v1.37 sneak peek flags kube-proxy's ipvs mode for deprecation, with a startup warning now, default-off by v1.40, and full removal targeted for v1.43. The same release removes the PreventStaticPodAPIReferences opt-out so static pods can no longer reference Secrets or ConfigMaps, and deprecates the kubectl run -f flag, giving platform teams concrete migration work ahead of the release.

title: Doc2CI: A Multi-Service Study of CI Configuration Generation Using Large Language Models
blurb: This paper introduces Doc2CI, a benchmark of 3,363 description-to-YAML pairs from four CI services, and evaluates 16 models across 53,000 generated configurations. Exact reference reproduction never tops 3.1%, and while 97% of outputs parse as YAML, only 71% satisfy service schemas, with larger models improving validity and code specialization offering no consistent edge. A training-free, schema-guided repair pass lifts schema validity to 94%, suggesting teams should treat structural validity as a distinct target from documentation similarity.

title: Source-Bounded Exact Recovery over Docker's Logs API
blurb: This paper defines source-bounded exactness for Docker log collection and shows that a persisted read position alone does not guarantee recovery after container lifecycle changes. Across 120 collector runs, a fixed LogDeck was exact in 60/60 while Grafana Alloy 1.18.0 managed 20/60, missing retained history whenever recovery required rediscovering an exited or restarted source. The takeaway for platform teams is that lifecycle reacquisition, not a saved offset, determines whether logs survive restarts.

title: TELLER: Non-intrusive Cross-Layer Root-Cause Analysis for LLM Inference
blurb: TELLER is a non-intrusive root-cause framework for LLM inference, stitching NVTX/CUPTI traces and service logs into per-request call-chain trees that span the engine, CUDA APIs, GPU kernels, and cross-node communication. It compresses each trace slice by over 80% with a Trace Pair Encoding tokenizer, then flags abnormal steps, localizes the suspect operator, and writes a plain-language explanation. The result is a triage layer for multi-node GPU inference where raw profiler timelines and logs alone miss cross-layer causality.

title: Agentic Self-Healing for Data and AI Pipelines: An Affordable Vendor-Agnostic Architecture using Open-Source Software
blurb: This paper argues that self-healing data and ML pipelines are an architectural problem, not a technological one, since the pieces already exist but sit fragmented across vendor-specific observability, incident, and remediation tools. The authors propose a vendor-agnostic reference architecture built on open-source and low-cost components, combining monitoring, pipeline metadata, deterministic policy checks, AI-assisted diagnosis, and approval-gated remediation so smaller teams can detect, repair, and learn from failures without paying for a ZeroOps platform.

title: AI Search Data Is Now in Google Search Console: Here’s What You Need to Know
blurb: Google launched dedicated generative AI performance reports in Search Console on June 3, 2026, giving site owners impression data for AI Overviews, AI Mode, and Discover AI features broken down by page, country, and device, with an opt-out toggle that carries no organic ranking penalty. The report omits click data and starts from May 18 with no backfill, so AI visibility is now measurable as a channel separate from traditional organic search.

title: What happened when 6.8m people were told real Monet art was AI
blurb: When X user SHLOMS posted a real Monet painting and labeled it AI-generated, over 1,300 replies trashed it as "obvious AI slop," "incoherent muddle," and "garbage with no sense of space." The reaction maps to what ASU marketing professor Andrea Morales calls the "effort heuristic": audiences reward work they believe took time and punish anything that looks effortless, regardless of quality. For marketers deploying AI creative, the lesson is that perceived effort shapes reception as much as the output itself, so how you frame provenance matters.

title: Snapchat will no longer recommend AI slop
blurb: Snapchat updated its Spotlight recommendation algorithm to demote wholly AI-generated videos, making "AI slop" ineligible for recommendation while human-made and AI-enhanced content still qualify. The move runs counter to Meta's Vibes app, which launched a fully AI-generated feed in February, and signals that platforms are now treating authentic, human-created content as a reach advantage rather than a constraint.

title: LinkedIn offers the option to report AI slop
blurb: LinkedIn is testing an in-stream option that lets members report posts and comments as likely "AI slop," using the flags to train its detection classifiers and privately warn creators when their content reads as inauthentic. The move complicates LinkedIn's own generative-AI push, and it is replacing the "enhance your post" feature with a lighter proofreading tool as it tries to curb over-automated engagement.

title: OpenAI ad experiment could change what happens after the click
blurb: OpenAI is testing ads in ChatGPT that launch a business-specific AI agent, letting brands answer questions, recommend products, and capture leads inside the conversation rather than sending users to a landing page. The shift threatens the click-to-site model that underpins paid search and dumps a new attribution problem on teams that measure ROAS by tracking what happens after the click.

title: From Information to Delegation: Mapping Human-AI Financial Decision Making
blurb: This paper introduces a framework that measures not just what people ask AI about finances, but how much decision authority they hand over. Applied to 1.5 million ChatGPT and Gemini interactions from 6,304 US and India users, it finds financial services are already a heavy AI use case, but consumers use AI to gather information and shape judgment rather than execute. The delegation gap gives PMs building agentic finance products a baseline: trust in retrieval is here, trust in execution is not.

title: Can AI Agents Simulate A/B Test Outcomes? A Validation Framework for Agentic Experimentation
blurb: This paper asks whether AI agents conditioned on behavioral profiles can simulate A/B test outcomes before spending real traffic, formalizing the idea as a Simulated Randomized Controlled Trial. Validated on 67 historical marketing tests, an off-the-shelf model captured directional signal (0.70 sign overlap) but overshot effect sizes, though a two-phase calibration cut squared prediction error roughly 77x. For PMs, the honest read is pre-vetting candidate treatments to prioritize which bets deserve live traffic, not replacing the experiment itself.

title: Coldcard Thefts Near $114 Million as Fourth Attack Wave Hits
blurb: Attackers launched a fourth wave of sweeps against Coldcard hardware wallets on Monday, pushing estimated losses to roughly 1,816 BTC, or about $114 million, since Thursday. The thefts trace to a firmware bug that shipped in March 2021 and undercut hardware wallets' core promise that on-device keys cannot be guessed, prompting maker Coinkite to release emergency firmware and halt shipments.

title: Ethereum researchers propose burning validator rewards to cap staking at 50%
blurb: Ethereum researchers proposed EIP-8361, which would gradually burn a rising share of validator rewards as the network's staking ratio climbs toward 50%, making additional staking progressively less profitable. The mechanism aims to cap total staked ETH without a hard limit, preserving liquidity for DeFi and transaction fees while easing consensus-layer overhead from an ever-growing validator set.

title: Wells Fargo joins JPMorgan and Citi in the race to tokenize Wall Street’s settlement rails
blurb: Wells Fargo will launch tokenized deposits this fall for select corporate clients, starting with round-the-clock dollar-to-pound transactions on its proprietary blockchain before expanding to more currencies and countries in 2027. The move puts it alongside JPMorgan and Citi, which already run institutional tokenized-deposit services to defend their deposit bases against stablecoins by keeping balances as insured commercial bank money on-chain.

title: BlackRock debuts tokenized share classes for select European money market funds with $311 billion in assets
blurb: BlackRock launched Ethereum-based tokenized share classes for select European money market funds, tapping JPMorgan's Kinexys settlement rails to move the roughly $311 billion in underlying assets on-chain. The move extends the tokenized-fund push beyond BlackRock's BUIDL treasury product into the higher-volume European money market segment, where on-chain shares can settle and post as collateral outside legacy fund infrastructure.

title: New Ethereum Proposal Would Burn Validator Rewards to Kill the Incentive to Stake More
blurb: Six authors including the Ethereum Foundation's Justin Drake published EIP-8361, "Tapered Issuance Burn," which destroys a rising fraction of validator rewards as more ETH is staked and drives net consensus-layer issuance to zero at a 50% staking ratio. Issuance currently supplies at least 93% of staking yield, so removing the yield floor lets the market, rather than the protocol, set the equilibrium staking level.

title: DEX Spot Volume Hit a Record 24% of CEX Volume in July
blurb: DEX spot volume reached 24.14% of centralized exchange volume in July, the highest ratio since The Block's data series began in 2019. The record share came in a shrinking market, as onchain volume held up better than CEX volume even while both fell and DEX spot totals dropped 26% to $130.77 billion, the lowest monthly figure since September 2024.

title: The $114 Trillion Question: How DTCC Is Tokenizing the Entire U.S. Market
blurb: DTCC, the clearinghouse that settles $114 trillion in US securities, demonstrated on July 15 that it can tokenize those assets, trade them in live production conditions, and convert them back without disrupting existing settlement rails. The pilot signals that the largest pool of traditional financial assets could move onchain through incumbent infrastructure rather than crypto-native venues.

title: COLDCARD wallet RNG flaw likely linked to $88 million Bitcoin theft
blurb: Researchers linked a random number generator flaw in COLDCARD hardware wallet firmware to the theft of an estimated 1,367 BTC, worth roughly $88.6 million, from 4,585 addresses. Block's analysis found an integration error caused ngu.random to fall back to MicroPython's deterministic Yasmarang generator instead of the STM32 hardware RNG, making affected seeds predictable in a 41-minute automated sweep that preceded Coinkite's disclosure by 30 hours.

title: Cloudflare kicks off stablecoin wallet rollout for AI agents to pay for APIs and online content
blurb: Cloudflare began rolling out programmable stablecoin wallets that let AI agents pay for APIs, data, and online content, starting with claimable wallet handles ahead of funding and payment features. Owners can cap agent spending by approved merchant, allowance, and transaction size, with micropayments settled through Coinbase's x402 protocol for account-free machine-to-machine transactions.

title: Mastercard completes BVNK acquisition to expand stablecoin payments infrastructure
blurb: Mastercard completed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK, a deal it agreed to in March for up to $1.8B, to connect crypto assets with its traditional payment rails. Mastercard plans to use BVNK's technology to help banks, fintechs, and enterprises scale stablecoin and tokenized-asset use cases across B2B payments, payouts, settlement, and treasury flows.

title: Western Union and Rain Launch Stablecoin Card in 37 Markets
blurb: Western Union and stablecoin issuer Rain launched Stablecard, a Visa card and digital wallet that lets money-transfer recipients hold balances as USDPT and spend at any Visa merchant or ATM across 37 markets. USDPT, issued by Anchorage Digital Bank on Solana and redeemable 1:1 for dollars, currently has 7.4 million tokens outstanding, with Western Union targeting more than 60 markets by year-end.

title: Hackers steal over $130M by exploiting bug in offline hardware wallets
blurb: Hackers have stolen roughly $130M in Bitcoin from Coinkite's Coldcard hardware wallets by exploiting a flaw that made seed phrases predictable, letting at least a dozen groups brute-force keys without ever touching the offline devices. The breach undercuts the core security premise of cold storage and adds to a year that has already seen over 200 crypto hacks and $950M in losses, per TRM Labs.

title: Every Bank Needs A Stablecoin Strategy: Sheffield
blurb: Visa introduced a stablecoin platform that lets banks and financial firms issue, move, and manage stablecoins, unveiled by Visa crypto head Cuy Sheffield on Bloomberg. The move positions Visa as infrastructure for bank-issued stablecoins rather than a competitor, giving incumbents a compliant on-ramp as deposit tokens and payment stablecoins gain regulatory clarity.

title: Coldcard urges users to move bitcoin as exploit is still in progress
blurb: Coldcard urged users to immediately migrate their bitcoin as an active exploit continues draining self-custodied wallets, with cumulative losses reaching as much as $114 million across an estimated 709 addresses. The flaw, dormant in firmware since 2021, lets attackers guess poorly randomized seed keys on specific Mk3, Mk4, Mk5 and Q devices, though wallets built with the dice-roll option are unaffected.

title: Bitcoin Bridge Boltz Halts Swaps Indefinitely, Citing AI-Assisted Attacks
blurb: Boltz, the non-custodial bridge routing swaps between Bitcoin mainchain, Lightning and Liquid, disabled its service indefinitely on Aug. 3, citing months of automated, AI-assisted attacks that outpaced its ability to patch. The bootstrapped team said contained exploits cost the company money but never put user funds at risk given its atomic-swap design, and cut off swap rails behind wallets including Bull Bitcoin and Aqua.

title: RWAs Topped Half of Hyperliquid's Volume for Two Straight Weeks in July
blurb: RWA perps topped half of Hyperliquid's trading volume for two straight weeks in July, doing $25.1B, or 52%, of the platform's $48.2B total in the week of July 13–19, the first time stock, commodity and index perps out-traded crypto pairs. The RWA category, run on the HIP-3 framework, is masking a shrinking crypto perps business as quarterly volume fell from a ~$1T Q3 2025 peak to about $550B in Q2 2026.

title: Announcing Cloudflare Wallets: the programmable wallet for the agentic Internet
blurb: Cloudflare launched Cloudflare Wallets, a programmable stablecoin wallet that lets accounts and their AI agents pay for APIs, MCP tools, and content over the x402 micropayment protocol. Users can claim a wallet handle for a stable identity and spin up Virtual Wallets for agents with guardrails like allowances, allow lists, and per-transaction caps to bound spending.

title: Wells Fargo to Launch Tokenized Deposits for Corporate Clients This Fall
blurb: Wells Fargo will launch tokenized deposits for corporate and commercial clients this fall, starting with USD-to-GBP transfers for select clients before expanding across currencies and countries through 2027. The move keeps payment flows on the bank's own balance sheet as stablecoins encroach, exploiting the GENIUS Act's carve-out that excludes distributed-ledger deposits from its payment-stablecoin definition.

title: BitGo Names Chainlink CCIP Exclusive Cross-Chain Provider for $7.7 Billion WBTC
blurb: BitGo named Chainlink's CCIP the exclusive cross-chain provider for Wrapped Bitcoin, moving more than $7.7B of WBTC off its prior LayerZero-based setup and making CCIP the default for all future BitGo-issued assets. WBTC is the largest asset to leave LayerZero since April's $292M Kelp DAO exploit, and BitGo cited CCIP's 16-operator minimum per lane, SOC 2 Type 2 and ISO 27001 certifications, and issuer-managed transfer controls.

title: Dinari launches tokenized S&P 500 stocks for US self-custody wallets using USDC
blurb: Dinari launched tokenized versions of all 700+ S&P 500 stocks, called dShares, that eligible US investors can trade with USDC directly from self-custody wallets through a Circle partnership. Each dShare is backed by a corresponding security held in qualified custody, though Dinari warned that thin secondary markets for tokenized equities may make positions harder to exit at a desired price.

title: BNY to add crypto staking to digital asset custody platform
blurb: BNY selected Galaxy to add staking to its digital asset custody platform, letting institutional clients earn staking rewards on assets held in custody without moving them to a third-party provider, pending regulatory approval. The bank, which oversees tens of trillions in assets under custody, has expanded its crypto services since launching custody in 2022 and is shifting transfer-agency record-keeping onchain.

title: Samsung is poised to become a dominant stablecoin distributor, analysts say
blurb: Samsung plans to add native stablecoin features, including fiat-pegged savings and payments accounts, to 800 million new Galaxy phones through Samsung Wallet, positioning it as a potential dominant distributor of tokens like USDC across 61 countries. The move builds on Samsung's 2019 crypto wallet, its nearly 19 million Wallet users in South Korea, and a $408 million stake in Upbit operator Dunamu.

title: Senators seek SEC probe of President Trump’s memecoin as crypto bill enters into a pivotal week
blurb: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal asked the SEC to investigate whether President Trump's TRUMP memecoin violated securities laws, citing reports that nearly 1 million wallets lost a combined $3.81B since its January 2025 launch. The letter lands as the White House weighs an ethics compromise on Trump's crypto ventures to clear a path for broad crypto legislation before the Senate's August recess.

title: Polymarket targets $20 billion valuation as competition heats up in prediction market sector
blurb: Polymarket is reportedly raising fresh capital at a $20B valuation, up from the $15B round it closed in April that included a $600M investment from Intercontinental Exchange. The platform, which says annualized revenue has climbed above $1B, faces intensifying competition as Coinbase and Robinhood add prediction markets and regulated rival Kalshi seeks funding at a $40B valuation.

title: Bitcoin losses from Coldcard hack could swell to $130 million, Galaxy Research says
blurb: Galaxy Research estimates losses from the Coldcard hardware wallet vulnerability could reach 2,000 BTC, or roughly $130 million, having confirmed 1,596 BTC stolen from 7,300 addresses across three attack waves. The exploit stems from a seed-generation flaw in Coinkite's Coldcard Mk3 through Q firmware, with 90% of stolen coins still unmoved as Galaxy works with US law enforcement and exchanges to flag attacker addresses.

title: Open USD rattled Circle's stock, but its key backers still support USDC
blurb: Open USD's launch, backed by Coinbase, Visa and Mastercard, wiped billions from Circle's market value and sent CRCL down as much as 20%, a drop it hasn't recovered from. Recent earnings calls tell a different story: executives at all three backers said they will support multiple stablecoins, framing Open USD as an additional payments rail rather than a replacement for Circle's $72B USDC.

title: Isabelle/STARK: A Formalization of zk-STARK in Isabelle/HOL
blurb: This paper presents Isabelle/STARK, a machine-checked formalization of a transparent zk-STARK proof protocol in Isabelle/HOL. The development includes an executable prover and verifier model, a finite probabilistic state monad with a weakest-precondition calculus, a zero-failure honest-completeness theorem, and a staged soundness theorem with an explicit probability bound. It targets readers with a formal-methods background, documenting the proof decomposition and the Isabelle source locations of the principal definitions and theorems.

title: Robinhood shrugs off crypto slump as Coinbase activity remains tied to trading cycle
blurb: Robinhood offset a crypto-trading slump with strength in equities and options, while Coinbase's volumes stayed tightly bound to the broader market cycle. The divergence reflects Robinhood's diversified revenue base against Coinbase's heavier reliance on transaction fees, leaving the exchange more exposed when crypto activity cools.

title: BitGo moves $7.4 billion Wrapped Bitcoins to Chainlink CCIP in latest LayerZero exodus
blurb: BitGo migrated $7.4B in Wrapped Bitcoin from LayerZero to Chainlink's CCIP, the single largest cross-chain messaging shift to date and the latest in a string of protocol departures. The move brings the total value moving from LayerZero to Chainlink near $15B, concentrating WBTC's interoperability layer under CCIP.

title: First U.S. spot bitcoin ETF to close as inflows dwindle, investors chase AI returns
blurb: Hashdex will liquidate its DEFI spot bitcoin ETF after Aug. 17, the first closure of a US fund holding bitcoin directly, after net assets shrank to $14.7 million against BlackRock IBIT's $47.08 billion. The move follows three straight months of net outflows across the spot bitcoin ETF group as capital rotated into AI-related assets, with BlackRock's iShares Future AI & Tech ETF up 39% through July while the CoinDesk 20 fell roughly 36%.

title: A new Solana proposal aims to ramp up daily SOL Burns from $47,000 to $650,000
blurb: Solana validators began signaling support for SIMD-0553, a resource-based fee proposal that would raise daily SOL burns from about 650 coins ($47,000) to as many as 9,000 ($650,000), alongside SIMD-0550, which doubles the disinflation rate to reach the 1.5% terminal inflation floor by 2029 instead of 2032. The linked proposals hold 24.94 million SOL in support and need roughly 40 million more to clear the 15% signaling threshold before voting closes Aug. 18.

title: SummerFi to Wind Down After Seven Years, Citing Exploit
blurb: SummerFi will wind down Summer.fi and sunset its user interface after seven years, attributing the decision to a recent exploit on its Lazy Summer Protocol that drained roughly $6M. The operator has not set a wind-down date or clarified the status of user funds, and its closure follows Zapper's planned Aug. 3 shutdown as DeFi front ends buckle under security and operating costs.

title: From Viral to Void: Multi-Dimensional Behavioral and Contractual Analysis for Rug Pull Identification
blurb: This paper introduces a multi-dimensional detection system for Ethereum meme-coin rug pulls, combining malicious contract design, on-chain transaction anomalies, liquidity manipulation, and social media signals into one feature set. The authors train an MLP with SMOTE oversampling and Focal Loss to handle class imbalance, reaching 0.927 accuracy and a 0.952 AUC-ROC on their test set. They ship a Flask-based tool for batch scoring and high-risk ranking, using the BOBU token collapse as a worked example.

title: Tornado Cash Logs 968 Deposits in Busiest Day of 2026, L2Beat Says
blurb: Tornado Cash processed 968 deposits on July 23, its busiest day of 2026, with the Drift exploiter contributing 78% via 23,095 ETH.

title: Flap Overtakes Pump.fun in Daily Revenue With $1.18 Million
blurb: Flap, a BNB Chain token launchpad, generated $1.18M in revenue on Aug. 1, edging out the $1.1M earned across the entire Pump.fun family for the first time, per DefiLlama. The BNB Chain flip is narrow and recent, with Pump still dominant over longer windows at $31.4M in 30-day revenue against Flap's $4.42M and over $1B in lifetime launchpad fees.

title: Crypto Card Volume Hits $748.7M in July, a Fifth Straight Monthly Gain: Paymentscan
blurb: Crypto payment card spending hit a record $748.7M in July, up 19.1% from June and 144.7% year-over-year, marking a fifth straight monthly all-time high across roughly 20 chains tracked by Paymentscan. RedotPay processed $395.1M, more than half of tracked volume, as stablecoin-funded cards keep setting usage records even while trading volumes fall to multi-year lows.

title: Strategy Sells 1,638 Bitcoin for $105M, Splits Proceeds Between Dividends and STRC Buyback
blurb: Strategy sold 1,638 bitcoin for $104.73 million between July 27 and Aug. 2, splitting the proceeds evenly to cover $52.4 million in preferred stock dividends and $52.3 million in STRC share buybacks. The sale, part of the BTC Monetization Program launched in late June, priced coins about 15% below their cost basis and leaves the company holding 842,138 bitcoin against a 12.00% STRC dividend it must keep servicing.

title: 'I Did Everything Right': Coldcard Victims Recount Losing Life Savings
blurb: A firmware bug in Coldcard hardware wallets made generated seeds guessable, letting attackers reproduce private keys and sweep roughly 1,816 BTC, worth about $114 million, from more than 5,200 addresses across four coordinated waves. Victims who followed the self-custody playbook, storing offline-generated seeds in safes and safety deposit boxes, are now racing to move remaining coins before attackers reach them first.

title: DCG’s Fortitude acquires 12.5 MW Nebraska facility for net $4.7 million, expanding Zcash mining portfolio
blurb: Fortitude Mining, the Zcash mining subsidiary of Digital Currency Group, acquired a 12.5 MW facility in Prosser, Nebraska, for a net $4.7 million in cash after credits, its third site in the state. The purchase, which includes land, building, and an on-site substation, lifts Fortitude's owned power portfolio to more than 60 MW across seven sites ahead of a planned public listing via merger with HeartSciences.

title: NEAR co-founder proposes protocol sovereign fund for long-term sustainability
blurb: NEAR co-founder Illia Polosukhin proposed a protocol sovereign fund that would hold NEAR tokens and route yield to public goods like validator support and MPC providers, rather than burning tokens to offset inflation. The treasury would launch with roughly 30 million NEAR, worth about $53 million, and could eventually move NEAR toward a fixed supply with lower effective inflation.

title: Bitdeer stock pops and drops on $4.7 billion AI data center lease in Norway
blurb: Bitdeer disclosed terms of a 16-year, $4.7B lease with Volta for 121 MW of AI computing capacity at its Tydal campus in Norway, sending shares up as much as 23% in premarket before paring gains to trade around $12.24, up 8%. An eight-year renewal option would lift the total contract value to roughly $8B, with Volta's obligations backed by about $1.3B in JPMorgan-arranged letters of credit.

title: Hackers Hit Bitcoin’s Safest Hiding Place
blurb: Hackers stole more than $100M in Bitcoin from thousands of accounts in recent days, marking one of the largest coordinated thefts targeting individual holders this year. The breach adds to a pattern of losses that has repeatedly hit retail investors, raising renewed questions about custody practices and self-storage security across the sector.

title: Fake World Assets Boosts Buybacks to 80% of Fees After Token Crashes to Record Low
blurb: TokenWorks, the two-person team behind NFT gacha protocol Fake World Assets, will route 80% of protocol fees to FWA buybacks and spend 327 ETH, about $610,000, on a team reserve after holders learned none of the $3.2M earned during launch was earmarked for buybacks.
