The reversal followed a selloff that drove FWA to a record low of $0.0066, down 78% from its July 26 peak.

title: Clarity Act sits idle over Trump ethics question as Warren asks SEC to investigate him
blurb: Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal asked SEC Chairman Paul Atkins to investigate President Trump's $TRUMP memecoin, citing an estimated $3.8B in losses across nearly a million investors and $636M in gains disclosed by Trump. The request lands as negotiators await the White House response to a Digital Asset Market Clarity Act provision that would bar senior officials from direct involvement in crypto projects.

title: Dinari brings tokenized U.S. stocks to American investors as equity race heats up
blurb: Dinari opened its tokenized U.S. equities platform to eligible domestic investors, letting them trade 724 dShares tokens covering the full S&P 500 via Circle's USDC across Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and Avalanche. The launch runs through Dinari's regulated broker-dealer and transfer agent infrastructure, intensifying a tokenized-stock race that Citi projects could reach $5.5T by 2030.

title: Marc Andreessen & Chris Dixon: Why America needs CLARITY
blurb: Marc Andreessen and Chris Dixon made the case for the CLARITY Act on a new podcast, arguing the crypto market structure bill now moving through the Senate is once-in-a-generation legislation that will determine where the financial system gets built. The bill passed the House last year with bipartisan support, and the pair contend that leaving the sector without clear rules is the costlier path for the US.

title: As Clarity Act teeters, mystery group hammers away at crypto in Washington ads
blurb: A group called Crypto Watchdog is running TV and online ads across Washington linking digital assets to terrorists and drug cartels as the Senate finishes work on the Clarity Act market structure bill, and its executive director declines to name the campaign's funders. The undisclosed backing arrives at the bill's most contentious point, where several Democrats and some Republicans have withheld support over its final provisions.

title: Bhutan's GMC puts part of its bitcoin treasury to work after 10,000 BTC pledge
blurb: Bhutan's Gelephu Mindfulness City hired Toronto-based 3iQ to run part of its bitcoin treasury on a market-neutral basis, shifting the reserve from a passive long-term hold toward yield generation. The mandate size and coin source were not disclosed, leaving open questions about the king's December pledge of up to 10,000 BTC and onchain data showing roughly $1B leaving wallets linked to Bhutan's sovereign fund.

title: U.S. FBI intelligence agent arrested in connection with theft of $1 million in crypto
blurb: An FBI counterintelligence supervisor with top-secret clearance, Patrick Yarmoch, was arrested for allegedly stealing over $1 million in crypto from wallets tied to foreign individuals the agency had investigated. Court filings say he pulled private keys from FBI systems, moved funds through Kraken and Sui's Suilend via a Slush wallet, and had booked travel to Portugal before turning himself in.

title: Bernstein says Texas data center audit could boost value of existing bitcoin mining and AI sites
blurb: Bernstein said a Texas state-ordered audit of data centers will intensify power scarcity across the regional grid, raising the value of bitcoin mining and AI sites with existing energy contracts. The firm argues that operators already interconnected to ERCAP capacity gain a scarcity premium as new entrants face tighter permitting and grid access.

title: Intesa Sanpaolo slashed IBIT stake by 94% in 2Q, tripled ether ETF holding as crypto prices slumped
blurb: Intesa Sanpaolo cut its IBIT bitcoin ETF stake 94% to 40,723 shares in the second quarter, gutting its call options and adding puts on 500,000 shares, while tripling its iShares Staked Ethereum Trust position to $7.1 million. The rotation tracked a rough quarter for both assets, with bitcoin down 14% against $4.89 billion of US spot ETF outflows and ether off 25% with $715 million of outflows.

title: South African lawmakers propose draft rules on cross-border crypto transactions
blurb: South Africa's National Treasury and Reserve Bank released a draft rulebook requiring that all crypto sent offshore route through an authorized provider and be reported to the central bank's Financial Surveillance Department. The framework builds on April's proposal to force asset declarations above a threshold and private-key handovers on demand, with public comments open until Sept. 30.

title: On Ten Yard Line On Clarity Act: Mersinger
blurb: Blockchain Association CEO Summer Mersinger said the Clarity Act, the landmark bill to define crypto market-structure oversight, is on the "ten yard line" but stalled by a dispute over which agency polices new ethics standards. A tight congressional calendar leaves little room to pass the measure this year, pushing likely resolution into 2027.

title: XRP holders can now borrow RLUSD on Ethereum through $280 million lending pool
blurb: Flare's wrapped XRP (FXRP) was approved as collateral in a $280 million Morpho Blue vault, letting XRP holders borrow Ripple's RLUSD stablecoin on Ethereum without selling their exposure. Sentora cleared FXRP under its institutional risk framework, opening a permissionless isolated market where borrowers mint FXRP through Flare's FAssets system, bridge it via Stargate, and take out RLUSD against it.

title: Cathie Wood’s Ark Invest snaps up nearly $10 million in Coinbase and Circle stock
blurb: Ark Invest bought nearly $10M of Coinbase and Circle stock, adding to its equity exposure to the two largest US-listed crypto companies as it rebalanced fund weightings during recent market volatility. The firm also trimmed a small position in Solmate, part of an ongoing rotation across its holdings.

title: Mastercard completes BVNK acquisition to expand stablecoin payments infrastructure
blurb: Mastercard completed its acquisition of stablecoin infrastructure firm BVNK, a deal it agreed to in March for up to $1.8B, to connect crypto assets with its traditional payment rails. Mastercard plans to use BVNK's technology to help banks, fintechs, and enterprises scale stablecoin and tokenized-asset use cases across B2B payments, payouts, settlement, and treasury flows.

title: BlackRock debuts tokenized share classes for select European money market funds with $311 billion in assets
blurb: BlackRock launched Ethereum-based tokenized share classes for select European money market funds, using JPMorgan's Kinexys blockchain to bring roughly $311B in assets on-chain. The move lets institutional holders settle and transfer money market fund shares directly on-chain, extending tokenization from cash-like instruments toward BlackRock's broader push to put traditional assets on programmable rails.

title: The $114 Trillion Question: How DTCC Is Tokenizing the Entire U.S. Market
blurb: On July 15th, the DTCC ran a live production test that converted assets from its $114T custody base into digital tokens, traded them, and settled them back into conventional form without disrupting existing operations. The pilot signals the largest US clearing and settlement infrastructure is moving toward tokenized securities, which would pull on-chain settlement from fintech experiments into the core plumbing of American capital markets.

title: Wells Fargo joins JPMorgan and Citi in the race to tokenize Wall Street’s settlement rails
blurb: Wells Fargo will launch tokenized deposits this fall for select corporate clients, starting with round-the-clock dollar-to-pound transactions settled on its proprietary blockchain and routed automatically through existing client interfaces. The move puts Wells alongside JPMorgan and Citi in defending deposit bases against stablecoins, keeping funds as insured commercial bank money rather than tokens, with programmable payments and multi-currency expansion planned through 2027.

title: India moves to give its instant payments network a business model
blurb: India introduced legislation laying the legal groundwork to end its zero-MDR regime on UPI, potentially letting merchants pay fees on some transactions for the first time since 2020. The shift would create a revenue stream for banks and fintechs funding the network, which processed 23.66 billion transactions worth roughly $313.4 billion in July, with Jefferies estimating merchant charges could add $525 million to $1.05 billion annually by fiscal 2028.

title: Cloudflare kicks off stablecoin wallet rollout for AI agents to pay for APIs and online content
blurb: Cloudflare began rolling out programmable stablecoin wallets that let AI agents pay for APIs, data and online content, starting with claimable wallet handles and adding funding and payment authorization later. Owners can cap agent spending by approved-merchant list, allowance and transaction size, and the wallets support micropayments through Coinbase's x402 protocol, letting agents buy access without a conventional account, subscription or API key.

title: Western Union and Rain Launch Stablecoin Card in 37 Markets
blurb: Western Union and stablecoin issuer Rain launched Stablecard, a Visa secured credit card and digital wallet that lets remittance recipients receive transfers as USDPT and spend the dollar-backed balance at any Visa merchant or ATM. The product is live in 37 markets targeting high-inflation economies, extending Western Union's onchain push, which moved $107.4B in cross-border principal in 2025, into a consumer-facing product.

title: Announcing Cloudflare Wallets: the programmable wallet for the agentic Internet
blurb: Cloudflare launched Cloudflare Wallets, a programmable stablecoin wallet that gives AI agents a stable identity and a native way to pay for APIs, MCP tools, and content via the x402 micropayment protocol. Account holders can spin up Virtual Wallets for individual agents with guardrails like spending allowances, allow lists, and per-transaction caps, pairing with Cloudflare's Monetization Gateway to build a two-sided market for agentic commerce.

title: Wells Fargo to Launch Tokenized Deposits for Corporate Clients This Fall
blurb: Wells Fargo will launch tokenized deposits for corporate and commercial clients this fall, starting with a limited USD-to-GBP exchange and expanding to more currencies and countries through 2027. By putting deposit liabilities on its proprietary blockchain, the bank keeps corporate payment flows on its own balance sheet as stablecoins encroach, using the GENIUS Act's carve-out that excludes ledger-recorded deposits from stablecoin rules.

title: BNY to add crypto staking to digital asset custody platform
blurb: BNY has partnered with Galaxy to add staking to its digital asset custody platform, letting institutional clients earn rewards on tokens without moving them outside the bank's custody, pending regulatory approval. The move extends BNY's crypto buildout since its 2022 custody launch, positioning a bank that oversees tens of trillions in assets to keep institutional staking flows inside regulated infrastructure rather than third-party providers.

title: The billion-dollar question: How will the neolabs actually make money?
blurb: The author examines how neolabs, the new wave of AI-native research startups, will convert frontier models into durable revenue rather than perpetual burn. The piece argues that API access and per-token pricing alone won't cover training costs, pushing labs toward vertical applications, enterprise contracts, and infrastructure lock-in. For fintech operators building on top of these models, the unresolved question is who ultimately captures the margin as inference costs and pricing power shift.

title: Every Bank Needs A Stablecoin Strategy: Sheffield
blurb: Visa introduced its own stablecoin platform, a system that lets financial firms issue, move, and manage stablecoins, and argues via crypto head Cuy Sheffield that every bank now needs a stablecoin strategy. The move puts Visa's rails and bank relationships behind stablecoin issuance and settlement, pressuring standalone infra providers and pushing incumbent banks to define a position rather than wait.

title: Dinari launches tokenized S&P 500 stocks for US self-custody wallets using USDC
blurb: Dinari launched what it says is the first platform letting eligible US investors trade over 700 tokenized S&P 500 stocks with USDC in self-custody wallets, through a partnership with Circle. Each dShare is backed by a corresponding security in qualified custody, though Dinari warned that thin secondary markets for tokenized equities could make positions harder to exit at a desired time or price.

title: Polymarket targets $20 billion valuation as competition heats up in prediction market sector
blurb: Polymarket is reportedly raising fresh capital at a $20B valuation, up from the $15B round it closed in April that included a $600M investment from NYSE owner Intercontinental Exchange. The raise lands as Kalshi seeks funding at a reported $40B and Coinbase and Robinhood add prediction markets, splitting the sector between Polymarket's crypto-settled model and Kalshi's federally regulated exchange.

title: Senators seek SEC probe of President Trump’s memecoin as crypto bill enters into a pivotal week
blurb: Democratic Senators Elizabeth Warren and Richard Blumenthal sent a letter Monday asking SEC Chair Paul Atkins to investigate President Trump's TRUMP memecoin, citing reports that roughly 1 million wallets lost about $3.81B since its January 2025 launch. The request lands as the White House weighs an ethics compromise on Trump's crypto ventures to clear a path for broad crypto legislation before the Senate's August recess.

title: Open USD rattled Circle's stock, but its key backers still support USDC
blurb: Executives at Coinbase, Visa, and Mastercard said on recent earnings calls that they will support multiple stablecoins, framing the newly launched Open USD as an additional payments rail rather than a replacement for Circle's $72B USDC. The clarification tempers a reaction that erased billions from Circle's market value and dropped its shares up to 20%, though analysts note existing USDC and USDT liquidity will matter more than Open USD's 140-plus launch partners.

title: Robinhood's Second Venture Fund Targets Y Combinator Startups in $200 Million IPO
blurb: Robinhood opened the order window for Robinhood Ventures Fund II, a $200M closed-end BDC that gives retail investors accreditation-free exposure to roughly 80 seed-stage Y Combinator startups, targeting an NYSE listing under RVII on Aug. 13. The vehicle pushes Robinhood's private-markets expansion into venture's riskiest tier, charging a 2% management fee plus 20% carry for total annual expenses near 4.18%.

title: Crypto Card Volume Hits $748.7M in July, a Fifth Straight Monthly Gain: Paymentscan
blurb: Crypto payment card spending hit a record $748.7M in July, up 19.1% from June and 144.7% year-over-year, marking a fifth straight monthly all-time high as trading volumes sink to multi-year lows, per Paymentscan. RedotPay processed more than half the tracked volume at $395.1M, and cumulative card deposits crossed $10B around July 1, positioning stablecoin-funded cards as a direct bridge from onchain dollars to merchant payments.

title: 10x Banking banks £40M in debt and equity raise
blurb: 10x Banking raised £40M in a mix of equity and debt from AshGrove Capital, its first fundraise since a £34M round backed by BlackRock and JP Morgan in 2024. The core-banking software provider, founded by former Barclays CEO Antony Jenkins and used by Chase UK and Westpac, will put the funds toward its go-to-market push after onboarding more than 10 institutions in the past year.

title: Robinhood shrugs off crypto slump as Coinbase activity remains tied to trading cycle
blurb: Robinhood offset a crypto trading slump last quarter as diversified revenue from equities, options, and its growing subscription and banking products absorbed the weakness, while Coinbase's activity stayed tightly coupled to the market cycle. The split shows Robinhood's push beyond crypto is buffering it against digital-asset volatility, whereas Coinbase remains exposed to trading-volume swings that rise and fall with token prices.

title: Hackers Hit Bitcoin’s Safest Hiding Place
blurb: Hackers stole more than $100M in Bitcoin from thousands of supposedly secure accounts in recent days, marking another large-scale theft in a sector repeatedly targeted by thieves. The breach revives scrutiny of custody and account-security practices as institutional and retail investors weigh how much protection self-custody and exchange wallets actually provide.

title: EU’s €5bn tech superfund officially open for business
blurb: The European Commission's €5bn Scaleup Europe Fund, managed by EQT, completed its legal setup and will begin investing within weeks, with a pipeline of over 100 startups and typical checks of €100m to €500m. The fund is reportedly in talks to back French AI lab Mistral and spacetech The Exploration Company, part of an EU push to keep late-stage capital and its fastest-growing companies from decamping to the US.

title: Samsung is poised to become a dominant stablecoin distributor, analysts say
blurb: Samsung plans to add native stablecoin features, including fiat-pegged savings and payment accounts, to 800 million new Galaxy phones through Samsung Wallet, which analysts say could make it a dominant distributor of tokens like USDC. The move leans on Samsung's existing crypto wallet infrastructure and its $408M stake in Upbit operator Dunamu, positioning the company to support both dollar- and won-denominated stablecoins as South Korea drafts its Digital Asset Basic Act.

title: Dinari brings tokenized U.S. stocks to American investors as equity race heats up
blurb: Dinari expanded its tokenized U.S. equities platform to eligible domestic investors, letting them buy and sell 724 dShares tokens covering the full S&P 500 with Circle's USDC through self-custody wallets on Ethereum, Arbitrum, Base, and Avalanche. The offering runs through Dinari's regulated broker-dealer and transfer-agent infrastructure, arriving as tokenized equities become the next real-world-asset battleground after Treasury funds, a market Citi projects at $5.5T by 2030.

title: Fintech: Why X Money Is Willing to Lose Money Today
blurb: X began rolling out X Money to US Premium and Premium+ subscribers, bundling a 6% APY cash account, a 3% cashback Visa debit card, and free instant transfers between accounts. The aggressive economics are a deliberate loss leader to convert X's 550M monthly users into banking customers, positioning the app as a distribution engine now folded inside SpaceX at a combined $1.5T valuation.

title: AshGrove completes £40m investment in 10x Banking
blurb: AshGrove, the €1bn European investment firm, completed a £40m investment in 10x Banking, the cloud-native core banking provider founded by former Barclays CEO Antony Jenkins. The capital funds sales and go-to-market expansion for a platform that now runs more than 10 million live accounts and processes transactions in real time as banks race to replace legacy core infrastructure.

title: Why Bridge's card program has underperformed despite Stripe backing
blurb: Bridge's stablecoin card program has underperformed expectations despite Stripe's $1.1B acquisition and distribution muscle, the author argues, pointing to thin merchant acceptance and unit economics that stablecoin rails have yet to fix. The gap suggests that owning the infrastructure is not enough. Card programs still depend on interchange, sponsor-bank relationships, and settlement plumbing that a crypto-native rail does not automatically improve.
